title: Amendment: stale grants mislead readers but never throttled admission; and the 12-subagent host ceiling is a separate limit from the charter 12
description: AMENDMENT to mha09 AGENT_GRANT_NOT_TRANSACTIONAL_WITH_SPAWN, plus a counter-refutation. Per capsule the active counts are 0-4, so no capsule is within 8 of the charter cap and no admission was ever throttled by the stale grants. The correct residual claim is narrower: grants are not transactional with spawn, nothing reconciles them against liveness, and the dag Active Subagents line therefore misleads HUMAN AND AGENT READERS - it did mislead me, and I propagated that error into briefs for three lanes. It does not mislead the admission gates. The mechanism in mha09 is unchanged and was reproduced first-hand; only the claimed consequence was overstated. PART 2 - COUNTER-REFUTATION, THE AUDITOR IS WRONG THAT THE 12 IS CHARTER-SIDE ONLY. The auditor reported that the 12-agent ceiling is charter-side rather than a host limit, on the grounds that .olt/charter.yaml:61 sets max_agents_in_flight: 12 and no 12 constant exists in the harness source. Both premises are true and the conclusion is still false, because there are TWO INDEPENDENT AND COINCIDENTALLY EQUAL LIMITS. Direct empirical evidence: attempting to dispatch a fifth orchestrator returned the host error "Concurrent subagent limit reached. You can run 12 subagents at once. Do not retry. If the user wants more concurrent subagents, ask them to increase CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS." Only the human raising CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS, or a live agent genuinely terminating, changes real capacity. Any lane told to clear phantom grants in order to regain capacity has been given a remedy that cannot work; grant hygiene remains correct for observability and for the transactionality defect, but it is not a capacity fix.

title: idleDuration measures the auditor own poll interval, making the stagnation predicate unconditionally true for any interval at or above the threshold
description: Quantitative demonstration, upgrading a previously code-read inference to a measured identity. At cognitive-auditors.ts:216-220 the liveness fusion computes lastActiveMs = Math.max(cursorMs, pulseMs) where cursorMs is the AUDITOR OWN lastInspectedTimestamp, which the auditor rewrites on every tick. Therefore idleDuration = now - lastTick = the polling interval, and with the threshold defaulting to 120 seconds (cognitive-auditors.ts:190-193) the predicate idleDuration >= threshold is UNCONDITIONALLY TRUE on every tick for any polling interval of 120 seconds or more, regardless of the subject Mind actual state. This is an identity, not a tuning problem. MEASURED EVIDENCE, verified by Tier 0 mind reading the ledger directly: the two writer repos each report a DIFFERENT constant, and each constant equals that repo own poll period. limo last 12 idleDurationSeconds: 170 180 180 180 180 179 180 181 179 220 139 180. skill-benchmarks last 12: 120 121 120 120 120 120 120 120 120 120 121 122. A genuinely stagnant subject would show monotonically GROWING idle time; across 76 samples spanning 4.6 and 7.6 hours it never grows, it sits on the observer own period. Two independent repos, two different constants, each pinned to its own poll interval, is the measurement reading the observer clock rather than the subject. The 7 undeclared gate ids referenced by those 9 receipts are gate-baseline-equivalence, gate-cli-entry, gate-export-surface, gate-no-suppressions, gate-test, gate-type-surface and gate-typecheck, while scripts-filesize-r2 declares only gate-split-simulators, gate-split-strip-comments, gate-extend-file-size-gate and gate-run-completion. The most probable origin is a plan recompile or supersession in which the graph was rebuilt with a different gate set while previously written receipts retained the old ids; nothing reconciles receipts against the current graph revision. CORRECTION THIS FORCES: scripts-filesize-r2 is NOT the clean positive control it was described as. Its honest figure is 2 receipts bound to declared gates, not 5 of 5 or 5 of 6. Remedies: validate gate_id against the current graph at receipt write time and refuse or warn on an unknown id; re-point or explicitly invalidate receipts on plan recompile rather than silently orphaning them; and treat a non-null gate_id as insufficient evidence of bindability in any audit, since membership in the declared set is the real predicate.

A tree-wide search for any check of gate_id against the declared gate set returns NOTHING. commandMatchesGate at gate-policy.ts:42-63 only ever compares against the specific gate it is called with. My previous entry warned that 'each new control revealed a class the previous one could not see'. This correction is different in kind and worse: I verified a measurement and then shipped an interpretation of it that I had not verified, in the same entry, without marking which was which. title: The evidence model can only record successes, so the question 'can this check fail?' has nowhere to live except inside a test process — which is the deep reason a gate must not be its own detector
description: Verified by coordinator_filesize-detector-r3b at command-evidence.ts:23: assertValidatorCommands rejects any cited proof with `command.exit_code !== 0`. A receipt that CORRECTLY exits 1 — a detector properly flagging a genuine defect — is permanently uncitable as evidence. The consequence is structural rather than a bug: an evidence model that can only record passes forces the falsifiability question inside a test process, because a bare run of a detector against a known-bad fixture produces exactly the receipt the model refuses. THIS IS THE DEEP JUSTIFICATION FOR THE TIER 0 DETECTOR/DEFECT SEPARATION RULING, arrived at independently and after the fact: a gate that IS the detector has nowhere to put the can-it-fail question. r4 is immune by construction — its meta-test spawns `bash <sandbox>/scripts/check/file-size.sh`, captures the exit 1 in-process, asserts on it, and the enclosing `bun test` exits 0 when all six cases pass. Every negative case lives inside the test file, never in a receipt. The coordinator has made that explicit and mandatory in its implementer's brief rather than leaving it incidental, with a standing prohibition on recording a bare run:exec of file-size.sh against an oversized fixture — that receipt would exit 1, be permanently uncitable, and burn lease time. RELATED FRAMING WORTH PRESERVING, from the same exchange and generalising well beyond this lane: the sibling lane's three `falsifiable: true` proofs are three readings from ONE INSTRUMENT THAT CANNOT SEE THE WRITE SCOPE. Proof count is worthless without instrument diversity. Also confirmed there: --resolve passes requireAllGates: false in record-review.ts, so commandMatchesGate is never consulted and a gate_id: null receipt can legitimately close a finding — applying gate-matching strictness to --resolve would produce false negatives on already-repaired tasks.
